The dark scheme and the other three shipped palettes are NOT covered. Zoomed images are nearest-neighbour 2x crops of the same captures, so a soft edge is magnification and not a rendering artefact. You rejected the previous batch on these grounds: the panes looked like a list box because they painted nothing. They paint now, which is what makes the question answerable rather than what makes the answer yes.

audit_verdict.note: Mechanically correct: qt_diff_workbench asserts the marking lands on the line the model places the group boundary at, and fails when moved to the group's own first line. Whether the placement is right is what you are being asked.

subjects.description: A hunk header cannot be a row of text here. These panes show whole documents side by side, so inserting a header row would make pane line N stop being document line N, and every mapping built on that equality would shift by the number of headers above it. The delimiter therefore has to be a marking on a line that already exists. I put it on the unchanged line immediately above each group, which is otherwise untinted. This is my choice, not one you approved, and it is the only placement the mechanism allows without custom viewport painting.
